summary: Louis Renou was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Paris and under teachers including Sylvain Lévi, Antoine Meillet, Theodor Bloch, and Alfred Foucher, later serving as professor at Lyon and Paris.

Louis Trolle Hjelmslev was a Danish linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen and under Holger Pedersen, Antoine Meillet, and Joseph Vendryes. He held posts in comparative linguistics at Aarhus University (1934–1937) and the University of Copenhagen (from 1937).

Louis de La Vallée Poussin was a Belgian scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Liège, KU Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden, and under Sylvain Lévi and Hendrik Kern, before serving as professor at Ghent University (1893–1929).
Louis-François Meunier was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Eugène Burnouf around 1848–1852 and Michel Bréal around 1866–1870.

Louis-Mathieu Langlès was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He studied at the Collège de France and served as professor and administrator at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from 1795 to 1824.

Louise Allison Cort is a specialist in Japanology and history/archaeology. She studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College, and served as curator of ceramics at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries from around 1981 to 2020.

Louise Child is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Leeds under doctoral supervisor Linda Hogan, studied under traditional teacher Ringu Tulku, and taught at the University of Leeds.

Louise Roche is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was affiliated with the University of Munich's Institut für Indologie und Tibetologie in 2023 and is attested as an assistant at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Gauhati University (attested 1999) under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma, having also studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.
Lourens P. van den Bosch is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Utrecht University, where his doctoral supervisor was Jan Gonda (attested 1978).
Lozang Samten studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.

Lozang Trinlae is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Northeastern, Harvard, and Claremont School of Theology, they served as CEO of Educational Visions and Methods (1993–2009) and visiting lecturer at the University of Tartu (2019–2021).

Lubor Hájek was a Czech scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Charles University under Otakar Pertold and Vincenc Lesný, and later served as Director of Oriental Collections at the National Gallery Prague (1952–1986).
Luboš Bělka is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from around 1977 to 1982 and held a post there beginning around 1993.
Luca Brigada Villa is a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and computational linguistics who has held posts at the University of Bergamo and the University of Pavia.

Luca Maria Olivieri is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the Free University of Berlin in 2011, directed the Italian Institute for Africa and the East, and was an associate professor at Ca' Foscari University.
Luchun Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who held a post at Ghent University in 2025 and is attested as a PhD researcher there in 2026.

Lucia Catherine Graeme Grieve was an Indologist who studied at Wellesley College, Oxford, and Columbia University (PhD). She taught at several female seminaries and colleges between 1883 and 1893, including Staunton, Frederick, Freehold, Mississippi Synodical, and Young's.

Lucia Dolce is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She has held posts at SOAS University of London as lecturer and associate professor, and is attested as a visiting researcher at Minobusan University in 2026.
